content:
Apple has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the latter of stealing trade secrets. The case has been reassigned to U.S. District Judge Edward Davila, replacing the magistrate judge who was originally handling it. Below are the details of the case.

Following the reassignment, the hearing originally scheduled for October has been cancelled.

When a civil lawsuit is filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, the case is randomly assigned to a district judge or a magistrate judge. If the case is assigned to a magistrate judge, all parties must indicate whether they consent to the magistrate judge handling the case in its entirety.

This is because district judges have the authority to preside over federal civil cases from start to finish, whereas magistrate judges may only do so with the consent of all parties.

On the same day Apple filed its lawsuit against two former employees, OpenAI, and io Products—Jony Ive's company—accusing them of stealing trade secrets, the case was randomly assigned to Magistrate Judge Virginia K. DeMarchi.

This means that all parties in the lawsuit must submit a form indicating whether they consent to Judge DeMarchi handling the case in its entirety.

Apple appears to have refused this arrangement. The company submitted a "consent or refusal" form yesterday (the form has not yet been made public), and this form appears to have triggered the process of reassigning the case to a district judge.

Since other documents explaining the reassignment were not available, there is strong speculation that Apple chose to refuse having the case heard by a magistrate judge.

The case has therefore been reassigned to U.S. District Judge Edward Davila, with Magistrate Judge Nathanael Cousins handling matters related to discovery.

Following the reassignment, the initial case management conference originally scheduled for October 13 before Judge DeMarchi has been cancelled and must be rescheduled before Judge Davila.

However, two other deadlines remain in effect: the parties must hold a settlement conference and discuss a discovery plan by September 22, then submit preliminary disclosures and a joint case management statement by October 6.
